title: LLM Harbor: batch ingest, transpile and canary framework
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a resilient, auditable pipeline (LLM Harbor) to support bulk intake of community weights, deterministic transpilation to Redwood runtime artifacts, automated validation + profiling, and a staged canary deployment that publishes pinned versions and performance profiles to the model catalog. Goals: reduce manual touchpoints in onboarding, shorten time-to-publish from days to hours for well-formed weights, and provide strong telemetry and rollback controls so downstream customers can rely on published pins. The pipeline will support batch submissions, parallel conversion workers, a smoke + deterministic validator, throughput/latency profiling harness, and a light-weight canary runner that exercises real inference load with synthetic and customer-derived prompt sets.
acceptance_criteria: Batch intake accepts tarball or HF-style repository and validates manifest signature and required metadata.
Transpiler produces runtime-compatible artifact and uploads fingerprinted bundle to artifact store with deterministic metadata.
Automated validation runs: shape checks, RNG-deterministic forward pass agreement on sample inputs, and safety filter smoke tests pass.
Performance profiler produces token-level latency, p50/p95/p99, memory peak, and cost-estimate metrics and publishes profile to the catalog.
Canary framework deploys pinned variant to a small dedicated pool, runs 1k synthetic sessions and 200 customer-sample prompts, and triggers automatic rollback on regression thresholds.
Model catalog entry created with canonical pin, compatible runtime tags, and release notes; observability dashboards and alerting hooks configured.
End-to-end flow is covered by CI e2e job and included in canary runbooks and runbook docs.
All created artifacts include provenance metadata (origin URL, submitter, checksums) and are traceable from intake to catalog entry.
design_notes: Preference for deterministic conversion: use single-seed export and shape-preserving ops where possible to make RNG agreement checks meaningful.
Use a fast-path converter for common formats (HF, safetensors) and queue slow-path (custom checkpoints) for extended analysis.
Profiling harness samples seq lengths using recent production distributions to avoid biased microbenchmarks.
Canary runner should be able to route a configurable % of traffic and run closed-loop QA queries from a secured prompt store.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (alpha): internal-only batch ingest of curated OSS weights; manual review gate before publish (Dec 2025).
Phase 2 (beta): enable automated canary runs for non-sensitive models with telemetry gating and ops notifications (Jan 2026).
Phase 3 (GA): open intake to community submissions with signed manifests and automated publish for passing models (Feb 2026).
test_plan: Unit tests for converter components (format parsers, weight-mapping rules).
Deterministic forward-pass regression tests against reference checkpoints with tolerance thresholds.
Load test the canary runner to ensure it respects per-customer SLOs and autoscaling constraints.
E2E CI job simulating full intake->convert->profile->publish path using synthetic sandbox weights.
risks: Conversion mismatches for highly-customized checkpoints that use ops we do not support; mitigation: slow-path human review and vendor collaboration.
Canary capacity contention with customer traffic — need rate-limiting and reserved GPU pools for canaries.
False negatives in RNG/determinism checks for models with non-deterministic layers — create 'fuzzy' signature mode and explicit approval flow.
Security/compliance risks from ingesting untrusted weights; mitigation includes signed manifests, sandboxed conversion, and KMS-backed keying for provenance.
